segments.text: When I was a child, summer vacations were special
Each year I would spend a month at my grandparents' house in the countryside
My grandfather was a former farmer with a large garden and fields
In the morning I would go out to the field with him to harvest the vegetables, tomatoes, cucumbers, corn
The vegetables that had absorbed the sunlight tasted different from what you buy in the city
Every dinner my grandmother cooked was special
In the afternoon we would go swimming in the nearby creek
The water was cold and the stones on the bottom
When I left in barefoot, it was so cold I fell breathless
In the evening, I would walk the dog with my grandfather
The Labrador Shiro was a wise dog who listened well to my grandfather
At night on the veranda, I would gaze at the story sky with my grandmother
Countless stars that could not be seen in the city would blink at me
My grandmother would quietly tell me the stories of the constellations after I moved to the city
For university
My chances to visit the countryside grew fewer
After my grandparents passed away
The house passed into other hands
But when summer comes
I still remember those countryside summers
Now as an adult
I take my own children to the countryside
Where my wife's parents live
There are fields, a creek
And at night a sky full of stars
Seeing my children chase insects
With sparkling eyes
And try to catch fish in the river
I feel my younger self
Is being restored
A country summer passed down across generations
There is something in it, but the convenience of the city cannot replace
